business_scope.primary_industry_name: Tier-3/4 Server Rack Space Leasing and Bare-Metal Server Hosting

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (unitary national jurisdiction; special economic zones include the Suez Canal Economic Zone)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — civil-law codification (Napoleonic tradition) with Islamic Sharia as the principal source of legislation; administrative justice is exercised by the State Council; no common-law system.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt-United Kingdom Agreement for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (1975)
China-Egypt Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 1994; in force)
China-Egypt Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (signed 1997; in force)
African Continental Free Trade Area Agreement (Egypt is a ratifying member; in force 2021)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended; Executive Regulation No. 1568 of 2002, as amended; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976; GAFI UBO declaration/registration requirements and the AML/CFT rulebooks of the Central Bank of Egypt and the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — UBO information is collected by GAFI and the Commercial Registry and is available on justified request to Egypt's Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit, tax authorities, courts and law-enforcement authorities; no general public UBO search.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity of each ultimate beneficial owner and each signatory officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority / notary public in the UBO's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization — Egyptian Embassy/Consulate legalization and authentication by the competent foreign Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Egypt is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, so apostille alone is not acceptable)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution or corporate authorization of any corporate shareholder/UBO approving the Egyptian LLC, shareholding percentages and appointment of the establishment agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (foreign notarization, foreign MFA authentication, then Egyptian Consulate legalization) and certified Arabic translation before the Egyptian notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the Egyptian attorney/establishment agent to file incorporation, sign documents and communicate with GAFI
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's home jurisdiction or Egyptian notary if executed in Egypt
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization plus notarized Arabic translation if issued outside Egypt

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Arabic Memorandum of Association of the Egyptian Limited Liability Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Egyptian Notary Public after due execution by shareholders/managers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal Egyptian notarization (not consular) and direct GAFI/Commercial Registry filing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds confirmation for the proposed share capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank holding the subscriber's contribution account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization and sworn Arabic translation if issued by a non-Egyptian bank; the bank must be verifiable through AML database checks

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory KYC/CDD under Law No. 80 of 2002. All UBOs, shareholders and managers must be screened against UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, the UN 1267/Al-Qaida and Taliban lists, OFAC SDN, EU consolidated sanctions, and Egypt's domestic terrorist asset-freezing list maintained by the Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit. PEPs, their family members and close associates are subject to enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval and documented source-of-wealth review. The low-risk classification for data-center colocation does not remove UBO disclosure or AML database screening obligations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Online Registration and Name Reservation Portal operated by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), together with the Integrated Commercial Registry portal of the Ministry of Trade and Industry; applications are made through the GAFI one-stop shop.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name of an Egyptian LLC must use Arabic script and include the Arabic legal suffix 'شركة ذات مسؤولية محدودة' (Limited Liability Company). A Latin-script transliteration may only be an auxiliary trade name and cannot replace the Arabic registered name. The name must be distinguishable in sound and spelling from existing names/trademarks; no contents contrary to public order or misleading as to the corporate form.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A reserved name may be extended by filing an extension request through the GAFI portal before expiration; extensions are granted at GAFI discretion, not more than two consecutive renewals, and may be renewed only while incorporation is still in progress. If the name is rejected, the applicant or its counsel files an administrative objection with the GAFI Legal Affairs Department within 15 working days, then an internal review before the Investment Registration Committee if not resolved. A further negative decision can be appealed administratively to the competent Minister and subsequently reviewed by the administrative court (State Council). A parallel alternative-name application is recommended to avoid delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not fully permitted: the LLC must maintain a real, identifiable physical registered office in Egypt capable of receiving legal process and official correspondence. Licensed serviced offices are acceptable for a business that leases third-party data-center rack space, but a P.O. Box-only or fully virtual address is non-compliant. If the only physical seat is the data center itself, the company must nevertheless have an office arrangement establishing the right to use that address and a local administrative presence for inspection and service.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but not negligible: approximately 5-10% annual probability of an unannounced inspection for a standard low-risk colocation LLC; 20-25% likelihood if the company registers through a serviced-office-only arrangement without operational substance, because GAFI and the Commercial Registry conduct post-registration desk reviews and spot visits; any VAT/tax audit increases inspection probability to roughly 30% and includes physical premise verification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: GAFI online name search and reservation fee for LLC
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Published GAFI service tariff for name reservation (non-refundable)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: GAFI one-stop establishment application fee (electronic filing and examination of LLC documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Published GAFI one-stop shop tariff under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Egyptian notarization of the Arabic Memorandum of Association and certified Arabic translations of consular legalized documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cairo Notary Public / Ministry of Justice and certified translation offices
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial page fee plus translation office market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registration of the LLC in the Commercial Registry and issuance of the commercial registry extract
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial Registry of the Ministry of Trade and Industry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory schedule under Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Stamp taxes on the memorandum of association and incorporation documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Stamp tax law schedule applicable to company formation instruments

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization of foreign UBO passports, board resolutions, powers of attorney and bank references
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular offices and Egyptian Embassy/Consulate in source jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official consular legalization fee schedule and courier expenses

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO database screening, PEP search and compliance file preparation by Egyptian counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External corporate counsel / licensed establishment agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for enhanced due diligence on corporate UBO structure

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year licensed serviced office / registered address and mail-handling service for the LLC
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed business center or office service provider in Cairo
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for serviced-address agreement, exclusive of office lease for data-center operations

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Law No. 176 of 2018 (limited liability company provisions, in particular Articles 1-3, 22-40, 51-57); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations; Commercial Registration Law No. 34 of 1976.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Corporate Registration and Investor Services Department (One-Stop Shop)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarised Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (System and Articles) submitted on GAFI incorporation Form together with the commercial register application
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to the Egyptian LLC; the Articles fix the capital, which must be fully subscribed and deposited into a temporary bank escrow account in the company name. The blocked funds certificate is submitted to GAFI and the capital is released only after commercial registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: This First Board Resolution of [●] LLC (the 'Company') is adopted on [date] by the founding shareholders. FIRST: the Company accepts the subscribers' share subscription and directs that the entire issued capital be deposited into the designated escrow bank account and remain blocked until commercial registration. SECOND: the registered office is fixed at [Address], Egypt, and all statutory notices shall be served there. THIRD: [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Name] is appointed Finance Director, and [Name] is appointed Head of Compliance, with authority per the Articles of Association. FOURTH: officers are ordered to file the incorporation documents, tax registration, social insurance, and civil defense licensing applications and to open bank accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name approval and legal form reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Services Centre / GAFI digital platform - Name Approval Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit at least three proposed company names in Arabic and English using GAFI's name approval form. GAFI will screen for similarity, prohibited terms and public order. Once approved, the name reservation certificate is issued and remains valid for 60 days; the same name must be used in the Articles.
required_dossiers: Completed GAFI name approval application
Copy of passport or national ID of each founding shareholder
Signing authorization if an agent acts on behalf of shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried for similarity, file an administrative objection with the GAFI Name Committee within 10 working days and simultaneously submit three alternative names to avoid restarting the process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and notarisation of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public (Tawthiq) - notary section competent for the company's registered address
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Arabic text of the Memorandum and Articles of Association, including corporate purpose, capital, share split, management structure and registered address. The shareholders appear before the notary to execute the document; the notary affixes the certification and returns certified copies for GAFI submission.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
GAFI name approval certificate
Passport or national ID of all shareholders
Proof of address or ownership of the proposed registered office
Power of attorney if a representative signs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary records a defect, execute a corrective addendum and re-attest the document before the same notary; GAFI will accept the corrected set if the addendum is filed together with the original.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank escrow account opening and paid-up capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate account in the exact proposed company name. Each subscriber transfers the subscribed cash capital into the account. The bank issues a blocked funds certificate showing the amount held for incorporation. The certificate must be valid on the day of the GAFI filing.
required_dossiers: GAFI name approval certificate
Certified draft Articles of Association
Passport or national ID of the signatories
Source of funds declaration
Bank account opening forms and specimen signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires a tax number before opening the temporary account, submit the draft Articles together with the shareholders' declarations and request a provisional corporate account under the Companies Law; escalate to the bank's compliance officer if refused.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI incorporation filing, fee payment and commercial registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop - Commercial Registry Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the full incorporation file to GAFI, pay the applicable registration and municipal fees, and await legal review. Upon approval GAFI issues the Certificate of Incorporation, extracts the commercial register record, and opens the tax file electronically. Shareholders may sign digitally through GAFI's safe electronic signature platform.
required_dossiers: Notarised Memorandum and Articles of Association
GAFI name approval certificate
Blocked funds certificate issued by the bank
Minutes of the founding general meeting appointing the first directors
Registered office lease or title document
Signed GAFI incorporation application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a non-compliance query, rectify by filing the missing document or corrected article within 10 working days; if the query concerns capital, provide an updated bank certificate and a board undertaking, then resubmit using the same GAFI case number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration, statistical registration and municipal operating licence filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) main branch, Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS), and the local district administration (Mayiya)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the ETA tax card application to obtain the tax card and employer file. Register with CAPMAS for the statistical identification number and apply at the local district office for the municipal operating licence for the registered physical address. Keep the lease and commercial register extract ready for inspection.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration extract
Articles of Association
TAX card application and Article 27 declaration
Registered office lease
Board resolution fixing the registered office and appointing officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax card is delayed, obtain a provisional acknowledgement from ETA and escalate to the ETA taxpayer service committee; if the municipal office queries the use category, present the colocation lease business description and the GAFI-approved corporate object.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social insurance, labour office and occupational health registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organisation for Social Insurance (NOSI), Ministry of Manpower labour office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with NOSI as an employer and obtain the social insurance file number. If initial staff have been appointed, submit Form 1/2/3, employment contracts and payroll records. For a data-centre facility, the Ministry of Manpower work environment inspection must be scheduled before intensive operations.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration extract
Tax card
Articles of Association
Passports or national IDs of shareholders and directors
Employment contracts for the first employees
Board resolution authorising the opening of the social insurance file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NOSI queries the block on capital, submit the bank release letter obtained after commercial registration; if the manpower office identifies discrepancies in job titles, file corrective declaration within one week and re-submit the list.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: General Authority for Industrial Development (IDA) for facility establishment clearance and the local district administrative office for the commercial facility permit; passive colocation does not require a telecommunications sectoral licence.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Facility Operating Permit (Tarkhees Mubani) and Commercial Operating Licence for Data Centre Colocation Leasing

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Environmental Assessment and Screening Report required for a data centre with backup generators; Category C - Full EIA requiring public hearing and technical baseline study if the facility stores hazardous waste or deploys more than the threshold capacity of standby diesel generators under Law No. 4 of 1994 and its Executive Regulations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater discharge for colocation activity; cooling water blowdown must meet Law No. 93 of 1962 and Ministerial Decree No. 44 of 2000 concentration limits; standby generator exhaust must comply with ambient point-source emission limits of Law No. 4 of 1994; battery and e-waste disposal must follow Waste Management Law No. 202 of 2020 and hazardous waste transportation and treatment rules; no solvent/VOC-emitting processes are authorised without prior approval

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by the Civil Defense Directorate under Law No. 80 of 2002; structural load clearance from the local engineering administration confirming floor capacity for server racks and raised floors; Ministry of Manpower occupational health and safety inspection clearance; commissioning approval for automatic fire suppression, smoke detection, emergency power supply and uninterruptible power systems; annual renewal of the civil defense and environmental permits.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — الهيئة المصرية للضرائب; unified e-services portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; mandatory e-invoicing and e-receipt platform: https://invoicing.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign owners may hold 100% of EG LLC equity (GAFI single-window incorporation; no minimum paid-in capital). SOP: (1) Incorporate the LLC via the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) or the Commercial Registry and obtain the Commercial Registration extract; (2) file the unified tax-registration application (Form No. 1 under Unified Tax Procedures Law 154/2023) with the competent ETA tax office (Mamouria), attaching the notarized incorporation contract, commercial registration, board/manager resolution, registered office lease, manager passports, and paid-capital evidence; (3) obtain the single Unified Tax Number (UTN) on the digital tax card, covering corporate income tax, VAT, stamp tax, salary/payroll and withholding obligations; (4) file the VAT registration application within 30 days of exceeding EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover, or earlier upon the first issue of zero-rated export invoices if input VAT recovery is sought — the ETA then issues the VAT registration certificate; (5) complete e-invoicing onboarding on the ETA platform: procure an ETA-approved digital-signature certificate, register the ERP system, pass API conformance testing in the ETA sandbox, and obtain the issuance code for the unique invoice validation/QR; (6) open a domestic corporate bank account and, if applicable, a Central Bank of Egypt (CBE)-licensed foreign-currency account to receive export proceeds.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — an Egyptian LLC is a separate juridical person subject to corporate income tax under Law 91/2005 (20% on taxable profits up to EGP 10 million; 22.5% on the excess); no pass-through or disregarded-entity treatment exists; distributions are subject to 10% dividend withholding tax; a non-resident shareholder is not taxed in Egypt on undistributed profits; the LLC income is taxed on a worldwide net-profit basis unless a treaty or statutory exemption applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt has no check-the-box entity-classification election; tax identity is fixed by the corporate-law form. Available statutory elections: (1) voluntary VAT registration from EGP 150,000 annual turnover (before the EGP 500,000 mandatory threshold); (2) presumption regime for small taxpayers under Law 26/2020 — eligible for turnover up to EGP 20 million, replacing net-income CIT with a reduced gross-revenue percentage (bracket-capped) and forfeiting input VAT recovery; the election is binding for three years; (3) Investment Law 72/2017 incentives — investment-cost deductions of 30%–80% for eligible activities, and/or establishment inside the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) free-zone regime where a corporate tax holiday of up to 5 years and duty/VAT exemptions may be granted by contract; (4) export support/refund election under Ministerial Decree 771/2018 for verified exporters of services, allowing faster refund clearance; (5) advance pricing agreements and advance tax rulings obtainable from the ETA for transfer-pricing and VAT characterization certainty; (6) fiscal unity/group consolidation and hybrid-mismatch elections are not available — DTT and permanent-establishment characterization apply non-electively.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 as amended by Law No. 17/2022 and the Unified Tax Procedures Law No. 154/2023; Executive Regulations Decree No. 66 of 2017 as amended; administered by the ETA VAT Department.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies (including zero-rated export supplies for threshold-counting); voluntary registration from EGP 150,000; non-resident suppliers of electronic/digital services to Egyptian consumers must register irrespective of turnover; all registered taxpayers are subject to the e-invoicing mandate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time central clearance: every B2B e-invoice and B2C e-receipt must be transmitted to the ETA e-invoicing service via REST API in the prescribed JSON/XML schema, digitally signed with the taxpayer's ETA-approved certificate, validated against ETA fiscal registers, and returned with a unique allocation code and QR before legal issuance to the customer. ERP-to-ETA API integration and conformance testing are compulsory; the mandate covers all VAT-registered taxpayers since 2023. Non-compliance fines range from EGP 20,000 to EGP 100,000 per violation under Law 17/2022, in addition to suspension of the e-invoicing code and the VAT certificate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 15 of VAT Law 67/2016 and the Executive Regulations, exported services are zero-rated where: (i) the recipient is a non-resident not having a permanent establishment in Egypt; (ii) the service is wholly or principally used and economically exploited outside Egypt; (iii) consideration is payable in free foreign currency and is received in Egypt; (iv) the supplier keeps a complete export file (contract, zero-rated commercial invoice, e-invoice with QR, and bank remittance evidence). For data-center colocation and bare-metal hosting, the ETA will test the place of effective use: the physical location of racks and servers in Egypt creates a rebuttable field-audit risk that the supply is locally consumed; the LLC must document, through the contract, data-flow maps, and operational evidence, that the non-resident customer's processing, storage, and management activity is carried out for offshore needs and that no Egyptian domestic traffic or Egyptian-resident data is served.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (only for re-export of tangible server/IT equipment; for pure colocation services a NIL goods declaration with the export-service schedule in the VAT return is used)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (where physical equipment moves across Egyptian customs; N/A for pure colocation service transactions)
Bank Inward Remittance Certificate from the receiving Egyptian bank evidencing full foreign-currency settlement of the export invoice
Commercial invoice in foreign currency endorsed 'Zero-Rated Export Services — Article 15, Law 67/2016'
Executed colocation / rack-space / bare-metal hosting agreement with the non-resident client, expressly allocating offshore beneficial use and excluding Egyptian-market service
ETA-validated e-invoice (unique QR code) and the corresponding export schedule in the periodic VAT return
Non-resident client tax-residency certificate or signed no-Egypt-permanent-establishment declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Assessment window: five years from the statutory filing date under Unified Tax Procedures Law 154/2023 (six or more years where no return was filed). On rejection of export zero-rating, the ETA will: (1) assess VAT at 14% on gross export proceeds; (2) add the monthly delay fine of 2% per month (month-fraction prorated) under VAT Law Article 51; (3) impose the fixed return-inaccuracy fine of EGP 300–5,000 per return; (4) apply e-invoice/e-receipt violation fines of EGP 20,000–100,000 per invoice; and (5) in fraud cases, pursue criminal evasion under Article 66 (imprisonment and a fine of EGP 5,000–50,000), claw back previously refunded VAT with statutory interest, revoke the e-invoicing code, suspend the VAT certificate and all export refund rights, and refer the file to the Tax Prosecution and the Economic Courts. Input VAT credits related to the disallowed zero-rated supplies are likewise reversed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — Banking Law No. 194 of 2020, Foreign Exchange Law No. 38 of 1994, and CBE circulars implementing the 2022–2023 exchange-rate liberalisation and interbank FX-market reforms
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains a managed-float but broadly liberalised current-account convertibility: trade, services, and profit/dividend remittances are convertible through CBE-authorised banks subject to documentary review, tax-clearance validation, and CBE remittance declarations. Capital-account operations (share subscriptions, capital repatriation, liquidation proceeds) remain routed through authorised dealers with CBE-designated purpose codes and compliance declarations; possible interbank FX-liquidity queues can temporarily delay execution. For the EG LLC data-centre colocation business, outbound profit remittance is permitted on presentation of audited financial statements, corporate tax filings, a valid Tax Clearance Certificate, and the applicable withholding-tax receipt on dividends under domestic law and the relevant double-tax treaty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory conversion/surrender ratio is currently enforced: since the 2016 floatation and the 2022–2023 CBE reform, exporters retain 100% of foreign-currency proceeds in Egyptian-bank FX retention accounts. Statutory repatriation obligation: proceeds from exports of goods must be credited through an Egyptian authorised bank within 90 days from the shipment date; services proceeds (including monthly infrastructure and colocation billing to offshore tenants) must be collected through the Egyptian banking system within the contractual invoicing period, with invoice and purpose-code documentation retained. Any routing of export or service receipts outside the Egyptian banking system constitutes a CBE/ECRA compliance breach and may trigger escalated AML review, suspension of outbound clearances, and Monetary Penalties under Banking Law No. 194 of 2020.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow / Operational Account and FX Retention Account
Capital / Operational Account and FX Retention Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. Offshore digital EMIs (FCA/EU-licensed) lack the CBE banking licence required to maintain EGP clearing accounts or settle through Egypt's interbank systems; using an unlicensed EMI for treasury flows risks Banking Law No. 194 of 2020 penalties, rejected SWIFT messages, and blocked inbound remittances. An offshore EMI may only function as a non-clearing collection or invoicing front-end; the operative clearing rail must terminate at a CBE-authorised bank account held in the legal name of EG LLC.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of at least one director or a designated local authorised representative is the de facto mandate at most tier-1 Egyptian banks for a newly formed non-resident-owned LLC; remote corporate onboarding is not uniformly accepted. Where remote onboarding is offered, banks require live video-KYC, authenticated (apostilled) corporate documents, certified passport copies, board resolutions, bank references, and in-branch issuance of e-banking tokens; a natural-person signatory resident in Egypt is still required for specimen-signature certification, ongoing audit queries, and handling of original legalisation documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) chain in the offshore parent group of EG LLC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO structure chart with corporate-registry extracts for each intermediate tier; certificate of incumbency from the parent's registered agent; audited group financial statements; certified copies of director passports; board resolution approving account opening, naming signatories, and showing specimen signatures; executed colocation/leasing contracts and tenant schedules demonstrating genuine economic activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High cross-border credit velocity in the first twelve months before the first corporate tax filing has been completed.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan covering data-centre rack capacity, power/cooling commitments, and projected monthly billings; executed colocation, sub-lease, and service-level agreements with tenants; invoices and payment schedules; lease or ownership proof for the Egyptian data-centre premises; parent bank's introduction letter and treasury relationship memorandum.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Geographic AML/FATF sensitivity of counterparties, including payments from restricted or high-risk MENA jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions-screening report on all beneficial owners, directors, and significant counterparties; AML transaction-monitoring statement; CBE AML/CFT Law No. 80/2002 KYC forms and enhanced-due-diligence file; engagement letter of the resident compliance/legal adviser; confirmation of compliance with Egyptian data-residency and data-protection Law No. 151/2020 for colocation service streams.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector or activity mismatch in the bank's occupation classification, such as data-centre leasing being misclassified as IT consultancy.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial-registry extract (Sijill) and tax card reflecting an ISIC 6209-aligned business purpose; formal lease and sub-lease contracts for colocation premises; landlord title deed or registered leasehold interests; rack-power, cooling, bandwidth, and cabling service schedules; tenant onboarding summaries and historical utilisation reports.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injection is processed as an inbound SWIFT MT103 credit to the CBE-authorised Egyptian account of EG LLC with the applicable CBE foreign-investment/capital-subscription purpose code embedded in the narrative. The receiving bank lodges the statutory inward-remittance declaration and verifies the transaction against the group board resolution, updated share-capital bylaws, Commercial Registry capital-update filing, and shareholder identification pack. Funds must be held in the designated capital/escrow account until the paid-in capital is recorded in the Commercial Registry; cash import, third-party pass-through credits, and offshore-EMI intermediaries are not recognised.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational and trade payments are settled via SWIFT MT103 customer credits or MT202 interbank cover, supported by invoices, contracts, customs declarations for equipment imports, and tax-withholding certificates; Documentary Letters of Credit (MT700/MT710 series) are the preferred rail for capital-equipment purchases from confirmed offshore suppliers. Each outbound instruction must carry the statutory CBE purpose code and satisfy the bank's transfer-pricing and tax-clearance screening; EGP-to-FX conversion is matched at the prevailing interbank rate on the value date. Dividend and profit-remittance MT103 instructions require the tax-clearance evidence and CBE remittance declaration forms to be attached at the branch.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (onshore, underlying commercial exposure, CBE-authorised bank counterparty, tenor generally linked to invoice or capex cycle)
FX swaps (spot versus forward principal exchange on USD/EGP or USD/EUR legs with a CBE-authorised dealer)
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term USD funding aligned to the data-centre build-out and lease-in receivables
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) — admissible only at the non-resident parent hedge overlay level; not bookable or cleared by a CBE-licensed onshore entity without regulatory violation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax (CIT) Return accompanied by the audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the close of the tax year; for a calendar-year LLC, on or before 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty up to EGP 20,000 plus 18% per annum default interest on unpaid tax; continued refusal can trigger administrative seizure, tax lien, and commercial-register strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Revocation or suspension of the tax card; mandatory regularization before customs releases, bank account transactions and issuance of tax clearance certificates; administrative fines apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Register Confirmation and Shareholding Movement Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) / Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 30 April and within 30 days of each share transfer or qualifying UBO change during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of EGP 40,000–100,000 for untimely or inaccurate disclosure; repeated violations may lead to registry suspension and compulsory strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Social Insurance Annual Payroll and Contribution Statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January of the following contribution calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-payment surcharge of 2–3% on unpaid contributions; fines up to EGP 50,000 and bank-account attachment for persistent default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Every Egyptian LLC must appoint a licensed statutory auditor and file audited annual financial statements under the Companies Law, with no micro-entity exemption; the volume of colocation lease contracts and capital assets of this entity independently require a mandatory independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) — aligned with IFRS — are the mandatory reporting framework for statutory financial statements in Egypt.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Egyptian Companies Law, the LLC must maintain a current register of shareholders and UBOs, record each transfer before legal effect, and file the transfer with the GAFI/Commercial Registry within 30 days. An annual confirmation statement, signed by the manager, is submitted with the audited financial statements, verifying that no unreported transfers or ownership changes occurred.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300–800 per annum for registered office, corporate secretarial services and government liaising
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500–6,000 per annum for a small-to-mid-sized data center and colocation leasing LLC, depending on transaction volume and balance-sheet size

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 50% CIT reduction for up to 7 years for qualifying investment projects under Investment Law No. 72/2017 located in the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) or selected development governorates; no data-center-specific tax holiday is statutory.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form Model 19) e-filed through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) online portal at eta.gov.eg
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months after the close of the fiscal year (Article 61, Law 91/2005); upon written request, a single additional extension of up to 2 months may be granted by the ETA; for a 31-December FYE the ordinary deadline is 30-April.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue derived from rack-space leasing, power and cooling pass-through charges, and bare-metal server hosting
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Egypt-source gross income plus any foreign income attributable to an Egyptian permanent establishment; ensure e-invoices support each revenue stream.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct cost of sales: bandwidth, power consumption, cooling, facility depreciation, and technician payroll
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only direct costs supporting Egypt-source revenue; allocate shared group costs on an arm's length basis with contemporaneous documentation.
Reconcile to the audited financial statements and maintenance of a cost-allocation matrix.
Cross-border management fees and recharges are deductible only with valid contracts, e-invoices, and proof of actual service received.
Align with statutory financial statements filed with the Commercial Registry and the ETA taxpayer file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: add-back of non-deductible provisions, penalties, entertainment, and taxes paid abroad
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back accrued but unpaid intercompany royalties, technical service fees, and provisions not supported by invoices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deducting prior-year losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 5-year loss carryforward cap; loss certificates from ETA must be attached where relevant.
Calculate on the final taxable income after all allowed deductions and incentives.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance tax payments, withholding tax credits, and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach ETA-generated credit vouchers and foreign tax credit certificates for income taxed overseas.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refund due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Settle any balance via ETA-approved bank channels and attach proof of electronic payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction declaration (ETA Form 82 / TP Disclosure Schedule)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory when related-party transactions exceed EGP 5 million per annum; disclose intercompany colocation sub-leases, equipment sharing, and cross-border management services.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-filing fine from EGP 30,000 to EGP 200,000; late-payment surcharge of 2% per month (equivalent to approx. 0.066% per day) on the unpaid tax, capped at 60%; incorrect or missing TP declaration triggers an automatic transfer pricing examination.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends paid by the Egyptian LLC to resident and non-resident shareholders (Article 85, Law 91/2005)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: File ETA Form 11 (application for double taxation treaty relief) at the Non-Resident Tax Office; attach the shareholder's Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the home tax authority, a Beneficial Ownership Declaration, the dividend distribution resolution, and audited financials; submit at least 30 days before the intended remittance; treaty rates on dividends commonly range from 5% to 15% for qualifying direct holdings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding: 20% on royalties and 20% on interest paid to non-residents (Article 56, Law 91/2005); applicable treaty rates typically reduce these to 10%–15% upon submission of TRC and beneficial ownership confirmation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Annual revenue of EGP 20 million triggers mandatory related-party disclosure; Local File is required when revenue is at least EGP 20 million AND related-party transaction value is at least EGP 5 million; Master File is required when the multinational group's consolidated revenue equals or exceeds EGP 200 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Article 44 (General Anti-Avoidance Rule) of Law 91/2005 empowers the ETA to disregard transactions lacking commercial substance; Investment Law 72/2017 incentive eligibility requires a tangible Egyptian presence, local staff, real infrastructure, and contractual revenue generation; a shell LLC without servers, metering records, or technical personnel in Egypt is exposed to full recharacterization of foreign colocation revenue as Egypt-source taxable income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional understatement of colocation revenues, fabrication of offshore lease agreements, false server-metering records, or destruction of billing databases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment for 2 to 5 years and a fine of up to double the amount of evaded tax (Articles 133–134, Law 91/2005); additional monthly late-payment surcharge of 2% on the unpaid balance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, general managers, and board members are jointly and severally liable for evaded tax, penalties, and surcharges; the ETA may impose travel bans, freeze personal bank accounts, and seize personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late Filing / Non-Filing of Corporate Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to submit Form Model 19 within the statutory 4-month window without an approved extension, or late settlement of final CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fixed fine between EGP 30,000 and EGP 200,000; monthly surcharge of 2% of the unpaid tax up to 60%; denial of the annual tax clearance certificate required for banking and government transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Article 147 of Law 91/2005, legal representatives are personally liable for the company's unpaid CIT and related surcharges where the omission results from willful neglect.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to present the mandatory TP disclosure (Form 82), missing Local/Master File documentation when thresholds are crossed, or pricing intercompany colocation services at non-arm's length levels.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA adjustment of taxable profits plus a penalty up to 50% of the incremental assessed tax; mandatory TP audit for repeated non-disclosure and publication of the taxpayer's name on the ETA blacklist.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face secondary assessment for the TP adjustment where the LLC is demonstrably undercapitalized or where documentation proves deliberate falsification of intercompany rates.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Utilizing a paper LLC to invoice colocation capacity without any physical data-center presence, concealing beneficial ownership, or accepting client funds without adequate KYC/AML controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under AML Law No. 80/2002, imprisonment for 3 to 7 years and fines from EGP 1 million to EGP 10 million; criminal referral to the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU); confiscation of proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil is pierced where the LLC operates as a pure shell; directors become subject to criminal extradition, travel bans, personal asset confiscation, and disqualification from holding board positions in Egypt.
